title: Segedin gulaš (pork and sauerkraut goulash)
description: Pork and sauerkraut slowly stewed with bacon, onion and lots of paprika, finished with sour cream. A continental Croatian winter favourite. Inspired by Serious Eats.

steps.text: Fry the diced bacon in a big heavy pot on medium for 8 minutes until the fat runs out. Lift it out.
steps.tip: The bacon fat is the cooking fat for the whole stew, so no oil is needed.

steps.text: Cut the pork into 2 cm thick slices, season with a little pepper and brown them well in the bacon fat, in two batches. Lift out and cut into 4 cm cubes.
steps.tip: Browning whole slices and cutting them after keeps the meat juicier than browning small cubes.

steps: Add the sliced onions to the pot and cook for 12 minutes until soft and starting to brown.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and paprika for 30 seconds, then add the meat, bacon, bay leaves and {1000 ml} water. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
steps.tip: A teaspoon of caraway seeds is the classic touch here, if you have some.

steps.text: Drain the sauerkraut and squeeze it lightly. Stir it in and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes more until the pork is very tender.
steps.tip: Rinse the sauerkraut once in cold water: it takes away some salt and sourness. Adding it later keeps it from going mushy.

steps.text: Mix the flour into the sour cream with a few spoons of the hot sauce, stir it into the pot and simmer for 3 minutes. Serve with bread and extra sour cream.
steps.tip: It keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.

title: Pasta e ceci (creamy chickpea pasta soup)
description: Small pasta cooked right in a garlicky, rosemary-scented chickpea broth, part of the chickpeas mashed to make it creamy. Cheap, fast and comforting. Inspired by Serious Eats.
steps: Dissolve the stock cubes in {1000 ml} hot water. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

steps.text: Warm {3 tbsp} of the oil in a pot on low with the sliced garlic and rosemary for 3 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Add the chili and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Gentle heat: brown garlic turns bitter.

steps: Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Mash a third of the chickpeas with a fork or a stick blender and a little stock. Add them to the pot with the whole chickpeas and the rest of the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The mashed chickpeas make it creamy without any cream.

steps.text: Add the pasta and cook, stirring often, until just soft, about 10 minutes. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
steps.tip: It should be like a thick soup, between a stew and a pasta dish.

steps: Off the heat, stir in most of the grated parmesan and the pepper. Serve with the rest of the cheese and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Crispy chicken piccata with lemon caper butter
description: Thin chicken cutlets in a parmesan breadcrumb crust, with a quick lemon, caper and white wine butter sauce and potatoes. Inspired by Serious Eats.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 minutes until soft. Drain and keep warm.

steps.text: Cut each chicken breast in half horizontally and flatten the pieces between baking paper with a rolling pin until about 1 cm thick. Season with half the salt.
steps.tip: Even, thin cutlets cook through in minutes without drying out.

steps.text: Set out three plates: flour, beaten eggs, and the breadcrumbs mixed with the grated parmesan. Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then crumbs, pressing gently.
steps.tip: Use one hand for dry and one for wet, so your fingers do not get breaded too.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan on medium-high and fry the cutlets in batches for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.
steps.tip: The oil is hot enough when a breadcrumb sizzles at once. Never leave hot oil alone.

steps.text: Pour the oil out of the pan and wipe it. Add the wine and boil for 1 minute, then turn the heat to low and swirl in the butter, the lemon juice, capers and chopped parsley.
steps.tip: Keep the heat low once the butter goes in, so the sauce stays creamy instead of oily.

steps: Spoon the sauce over the cutlets just before eating, so the crust stays crisp. Serve with the potatoes.

title: Gambas al ajillo (Spanish garlic prawns)
description: Prawns sizzled in olive oil with lots of garlic and a little chili, finished with vinegar and parsley. Serve with bread for the garlic oil. Inspired by Serious Eats.

steps.text: Thaw the prawns if frozen and pat them dry. Mix them with a third of the garlic (finely chopped), {1 tbsp} of the oil, the salt and baking soda.
steps.tip: The pinch of soda keeps prawns plump and snappy.

steps.text: Slice the rest of the garlic thinly. Warm it with the rest of the oil and the chili in a frying pan on low for 4 minutes until pale gold.
steps.tip: Watch it: once garlic turns brown it tastes bitter.

steps.text: Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the prawns and toss for 2 minutes until pink all over.
steps.tip: They are done the moment they turn pink and curl. Any longer and they go rubbery.

steps: Take off the heat, stir in the vinegar and parsley and serve straight away in the pan, with bread to dip in the oil.

title: Cheesy tuna and sweetcorn pasta bake
description: Pasta in a homemade cheese sauce with tuna and sweetcorn, baked until bubbling and golden. A family classic from the cupboard. Inspired by BBC Good Food.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain.
steps.tip: It finishes cooking in the oven, so it stays firm instead of going soft.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 5 minutes, whisking, until thick and smooth.
steps.tip: Adding the milk slowly while whisking is how you get a sauce without lumps.

steps: Off the heat, stir in three quarters of the grated cheese, the salt and pepper.
Mix the sauce with the pasta, drained tuna, drained sweetcorn and chopped parsley and tip it into a baking dish. Scatter the rest of the cheese on top.

steps.text: Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden.
steps.tip: Gouda works instead of cheddar. It keeps 3 days and freezes well in portions.

title: Mushroom stroganoff with rice
description: Well-browned mushrooms in a paprika and sour cream sauce, ready in 30 minutes, over rice. Inspired by BBC Good Food.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Soften the chopped onions in the oil in a large frying pan for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Stir in the paprika and garlic for 30 seconds, then add the sliced mushrooms. Turn the heat up and cook for 8 minutes until they are browned and their liquid has gone.
steps.tip: Do not stir too often. Browned mushrooms taste meaty; pale ones taste watery.

steps: Dissolve the stock cube in {300 ml} hot water. Add it with the soy sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream and salt. Scatter with parsley and serve over the rice.
steps.tip: Adding the sour cream off the heat keeps the sauce smooth instead of splitting.

title: Caldo verde (potato, kale and sausage soup)
description: The Portuguese soup of potatoes, finely shredded kale and smoked sausage, part of the potato crushed to make it creamy. Inspired by Serious Eats.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and sliced garlic in the butter and {1 tbsp} of the oil in a big pot for 5 minutes.
Peel and thinly slice the potatoes. Add them with the stock cubes and {1500 ml} water and bring to a simmer.

steps.text: Strip the kale leaves from the stems, roll them up and slice them into very thin ribbons. Add them to the pot and simmer for 25 minutes.
steps.tip: Thin ribbons are the secret: they turn silky instead of chewy.

steps.text: Crush some of the potatoes against the side of the pot with a spoon to thicken the soup, leaving the rest in pieces.
steps.tip: Two textures make it creamy without blending.

steps.text: Slice the sausages and add them for the last 5 minutes to warm through. Season with pepper and serve with a drizzle of the rest of the olive oil and bread.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days. Taste before adding salt: the sausage and stock are already salty.

title: Egg roll in a bowl (turkey and cabbage stir-fry)
description: All the flavours of a spring roll filling with no rolling or frying: minced turkey, mushrooms, cabbage and carrot in a ginger soy dressing, over rice. Inspired by Budget Bytes.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps.text: Chop the mushrooms very finely, shred the cabbage and grate the carrots.
steps.tip: Finely chopped mushrooms melt into the meat and stretch it further.

steps: Brown the turkey in the oil in a wok or large frying pan on high for 8 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the chopped onion, mushrooms, garlic and grated ginger and cook for 4 minutes until the mushroom water has gone.

steps.text: Add the cabbage and carrot and stir-fry for 5 minutes until softened but still a little crunchy.
steps.tip: Do not cook it until limp: a bit of crunch is the point.

steps: Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil, pour it in and toss for 2 minutes. Serve over the rice with sliced spring onion.

title: Honey garlic salmon with rice and broccoli
description: Salmon seared golden and glazed in a sticky honey, soy and garlic sauce in the last minute, with rice and broccoli. Ready in 20 minutes. Inspired by RecipeTin Eats.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {250 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Cut the broccoli into florets and steam or boil them for 4 minutes.
Pat the salmon dry and season with pepper. Whisk the honey, soy sauce, vinegar and finely chopped garlic in a cup.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan on medium-high and fry the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then turn and cook for 2 minutes more.
steps.tip: Leave it alone while it browns. It releases from the pan by itself when it is ready to turn.

steps.text: Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 1 minute, spooning it over the fish until sticky.
steps.tip: The glaze goes in only at the end: honey burns quickly.

steps: Serve on the rice with the broccoli, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Basque burnt cheesecake
description: A crustless cheesecake baked very hot, so the top turns dark and caramelised while the middle stays soft and creamy. Easier than it looks. Inspired by RecipeTin Eats.

steps.text: Take the cream cheese, cream and eggs out of the fridge an hour before. Heat the oven to 220 °C. Line a 20 cm deep round tin with two crumpled sheets of baking paper, sticking up well above the sides.
steps.tip: Crumple the paper into a ball first, then flatten it: it fits the tin much better.

steps.text: Beat the cream cheese with the sugar, vanilla sugar and salt until completely smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
steps.tip: Room-temperature cream cheese is the key to no lumps.

steps: Whisk the flour into a little of the cream until smooth, then beat it in with the rest of the cream.

steps.text: Pour into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until the top is very dark brown and the middle still wobbles a lot when you shake the tin.
steps.tip: The dark top is meant to be, it is not burnt. The wobbly middle sets as it cools.

steps.text: Cool in the tin for 2 hours, then chill for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, before cutting.
steps.tip: It keeps 4 days in the fridge. Lovely with berries.
